beats.text: One. Failure is information, not identity. It tells you what to adjust — not who you are.
Two. You never controlled the outcome, only the effort. Judge yourself on the part that was yours.
Three. The obstacle is the way. What blocks the path becomes the material you build with.
Four. Shame is optional. Only your own wrongdoing is truly shameful — a lost attempt isn't.
Five. Fall seven times, rise eight — and make sure you keep your principles on the way up.
The Stoic doesn't fear failing. He fears only becoming someone who stopped trying to be good.
